question: Is adding sealed MultiWriterTopic<T> between Topic<T> and EventTopic<T>/ReplayTopic<T> a compatible amendment of topic-model@v1, or a breaking one that needs v2 (and so a run stop)?

options.label: amend v1 compatibly
options.consequence: Keeps topic-model@v1; bus-api@v1's Interface and fixtures compile as written. Accepts one changed inference result (the least upper bound of an event and a replay topic) as outside the declared surface.

options.label: draft topic-model@v2
options.consequence: Treats the inference change as breaking: a v2 with a migration note for a draft contract with no producer or consumer code, and every consumer contract re-pointed at v2.

options.label: report a breaking-amend run stop
options.consequence: Ends the run until the owner rules on whether an inference-only change counts as breaking.

chosen: amend v1 compatibly
why: The experiment replays every topic-model@v1 fixture as it stood at df5e8f8 against a stand-in carrying the amendment: structure, surface, reject and all 40 behavior cases pass (A1 to A4), exactly as against the stand-in without it (D1). topology-dsl@v1's and topology-ir@v1's surface and reject sets, and topology-dsl@v1's recorder suite, give identical results against both stand-ins (C1, C2, D3). No leaf variant is added, so the three-variant exhaustive switch in the existing surface and G1's non-exhaustive reject keep their results; seeded defect M1 shows that this holds only because the intermediate is sealed (an abstract one makes the existing three-variant switch non-exhaustive). One source-level effect exists and is recorded in the contract's Versioning: the least upper bound of EventTopic<int> and ReplayTopic<int> moves from Topic<int> to MultiWriterTopic<int>, so `final mixed = [event, replay]; mixed.add(state);` compiles before and fails after (probe/lub.dart, C3 against D4). That is the same class of edge the Versioning section already accepts as compatible (a new top-level function can collide with a consumer's import; a new getter can shadow a consumer's extension member), it touches no type the Interface states, no consumer code exists (every contract is draft, no package exists), and no existing fixture hits it. Signal that would have changed my mind: a consumer fixture or contract text that relies on the inferred type of such a mix, or the contract being stable with code already built against it.
evidence: hsdd/contract/topic-model.md ## Versioning (pre-existing Breaking and Compatible lists)

question: Fold in S07's note: state the lineage a state topic's initial value carries when it is first observed or read? If so, which lineage?

question: OQ-R2, first half (Guide §10.1 'Envelope recording'): what is the envelope recorder's assertion API: pattern matching, equality, custom predicates?

options.label: typed queries returning plain values
options.consequence: envelopes, envelopesOf(topic) and payloadsOf(topic) return unmodifiable lists typed by the topic; tests use ==, Dart 3 patterns and Iterable.where with their runner's expect; no new dependency; failure messages are whatever expect prints

options.label: package:matcher matchers over envelopes
options.consequence: richer failure messages (isEnvelope(payload: ..., source: ...)), but nidana_dart_runtime gains a dependency that ADR-002 item 3's table and bus-api@v1 G39 do not list, so a bus-api amendment and a runtime D{n} would follow

options.label: a predicate DSL of its own
options.consequence: a vocabulary to learn and maintain that Dart patterns already cover

chosen: typed queries returning plain values
why: Dart 3 already gives equality, destructuring patterns and predicates over values, so the recorder only has to hand out typed values; the cast from MessageEnvelope<Object?> to the topic's type is the one thing tests cannot write conveniently, and envelopesOf/payloadsOf do it. Deterministic ids and the fixed initial time (G13) make whole-envelope equality usable. The owner's preference for values and composition over DSLs points the same way, and the runtime's dependency set stays as ADR-002 and bus-api@v1 G39 fix it. Signal that would change it: app teams writing the same envelope matchers in several test suites; matchers can then ship as a compatible addition in a separate library.

question: OQ-R2, second half (Guide §10.1 'Topology test isolation'): how does a test activate only the topologies under test without the APPLICATION set?

options.label: TestBus activates nothing; input and stub helpers stand in for absent producers
options.consequence: isolation is the default; TestBus.input (a publisher of ServiceSource('test')) and TestBus.stub(topic) (a writer claiming one state topic at application scope) replace the boilerplate every test would write; two more members and one guarantee

options.label: documented pattern only, no helpers
options.consequence: smallest surface; every test constructs its own publishers and claims, as bus-api@v1's live binding does by hand

options.label: a selective activation API over an app bootstrap
options.consequence: a TestBus that runs the app's bootstrap and ignores activations not listed; couples tests to the bootstrap and hides which topologies are active

chosen: TestBus activates nothing; input and stub helpers stand in for absent producers
why: On this tree activation is always explicit (bus-api@v1 G22, G34): a fresh TestBus has nothing active, so the Guide's question reduces to standing in for the producers that are absent, as hsdd/spec/nidana.runtime.md's OQ-R2 detail already observes. The stand-in for a state topic must claim it (Spec §2.4, §3.11), which is the boilerplate bus-api@v1's bus_activation_test.dart writes by hand; stub makes it one call, claims at Scope.application so it never trips the scope check, and claims one topic per publisher so stubs never conflict with each other. Close to the no-helper option; the signal that would change it is a consumer for whom a fixed ServiceSource('test') source is wrong.

question: Spec §9.2 item 2: the TestBus envelope recorder defaults to redacting sensitive payloads, raw view by explicit opt-in. Where does the opt-in live, given that bus-api@v1's bindings read recorder.envelopes and RecordedEnvelope.envelope?

options.label: per read: RecordedEnvelope.unredacted and an unredacted: true argument on the typed queries
options.consequence: envelope is unredacted.redacted(), so non-sensitive envelopes are the delivered objects and bus-api@v1's bindings work unchanged; typed queries on a sensitive topic throw ArgumentError without the argument; every raw read is visible at its call site

options.label: per recorder, a flag at TestBus construction
options.consequence: not expressible as a named parameter, because TestBus([BusConfig config]) already has an optional positional parameter and Dart cannot mix the two; would need a BusConfig field that bus-api@v1 owns

options.label: a separate raw view object (recorder.unredacted)
options.consequence: two parallel query surfaces to keep in step

question: Does a TestBus generate deterministic envelope ids (bus-api@v1 says only that ids are opaque and pairwise distinct)?

options.consequence: nothing to state, but envelope equality is unusable in tests

question: OQ-N2: Do routes carry typed arguments (Route<Args>) or untyped maps?

options.consequence: compile-time checking of an intent's arguments against its route; RouteState equality and nav.current-route dedup work through the app's value types; deep-link resolvers and redirects build typed arguments; arguments are not required at the call, as the Guide's are not

options.label: untyped Map<String, Object?> arguments
options.consequence: the Guide §3.2 sketch; no checking; Dart maps have no value equality, so equal RouteStates compare unequal and the topic's default dedup never fires; destinations cast

options.consequence: presence is checked too, at the cost of two route types and the registry complexity Guide §3.2 warns about

why: Owner's standing preference for types and ADTs, Spec §4.2's compile-time typing for topics as the analogue, and a Dart-specific reason the Guide does not weigh: map arguments break RouteState equality (Spec §3.12 dedup is Dart ==). question: After the connection, does every later delivery reach a topology's read during that delivery, so the deliveries start() makes reach a topology's reads in queue order across topics? chosen: pin it: a connected read receives each later delivery during that delivery
